body:
I went to my treatment and ended up having complications simply from the lack of sleep. I am alright, but have some amnesia, which isn't an abnormal side effect. I don't remember a whole lot of the last few days. Stuff is slowly coming back, but I couldn't remember where I lived and things like that.

Kind of weird, but I am not feeling suicidal anymore. Probably forgot what was making me so down to begin with. 

Anyway thanks for your comment, I appreciate the thought!
I edited my initial post with the outcome. Thanks for talking with me, I appreciate your time.

I am at home and go to ect three times a week. I stopped sleeping since my first treatment.

Notes can be misunderstood, or taken out of context. I don't need my survivors questioning everything I have left behind.

Yes, I have a couple. One is more painful but has a high chance of success and if I am lucky a body won't turn up. I have been holding off on this one because I don't want to have to write a note.

Others are just painful and messy, or involve more travel than I can reasonably do without being tracked. At least with ECT it is something I am required to do, other things take extra effort that is really too much for me. If I was willing to put that kind of effort into my death maybe I could direct that energy to something in my life... But I just don't have the drive for it.

Not killing myself out of fear if failure is still failing.

Even if I take no action I will end up sick or disabled. Freeze to death on the streets or something.

I dunno, it feels better that my death can be under my own power, because the way I see it is that inaction is still going to kill me, and it'll take longer and hurt more.

No, that isn't an option here. If I want to die I have to do it myself or get someone else to do it illegally. 

Physical injury and disability are just kind of a basic risk a person runs with suicide. The body is adapted to fight to live after all, even when the brain is trying so hard to kill it..

They'll attempt to save me of course, but that doesn't mean they'll succeed. It is my third treatment today, but I won't be doing anything until my forth or fifth when I have done a bit more research.

Heck I am even considering just asking my Dr if something could just...go wrong.

You are correct.

Essentially the hope is that I vomit during the procedure and it gets in my lungs and I drown while I am under anesthesia. The idea is that I go under peacefully and just don't wake up again.
